minutes.headline: Select Board agreed a new open process for appointed-board terms: public notice, input from chairs, all candidates heard together.
minutes.summary: The board ratified a reserve police officer appointment, approved minutes, and heard updates on a water district expansion meeting and a second cannabis outreach meeting. Most of the night was a workshop on a new annual process for appointing and reappointing members of town boards. The workshop was left unfinished and tabled until the full board returns, with the chair to write up what was agreed.

decisions.decision: Step two of the appointment process: the executive assistant emails the list of expiring terms to the select board, town manager, appointed-committee chairs and the members whose terms expire.
Members whose terms expire must state in writing (electronic or paper) to the select board whether they want to be considered again.
The published list of expiring positions will say whether the current member is seeking reappointment.
Current committees and chairs are encouraged, not required, to give input on reappointments, without a formal vote; the public is also invited to comment.
Incumbents and new applicants will be considered together, at the same time, rather than incumbents first.
New applicants are encouraged but not required to attend a meeting of the body they want to join.
Contested seats should be interviewed on the same evening where possible; appointments are targeted for the first select board meetings in June.
The appointment process workshop was halted and tabled until the other two members return; the chair will write up what was agreed and circulate it.
Water district superintendent invited to meet the board March 2 or 9; awaiting reply.
Second Green Leaf community outreach meeting scheduled for March 10, to be on the town's Zoom.

what_happened.line: The Select Board spent most of the night on a workshop for a new yearly process to appoint and reappoint members of town boards, and tabled it unfinished.
The workshop agreed that incumbents and new applicants are considered together, not incumbents first, and contested seats are interviewed the same evening where possible.
Members with expiring terms must say in writing whether they want to be considered again, and the published list of expiring seats will show it.
Committee chairs are encouraged, not required, to give input on reappointments with no formal vote, and the public may comment; appointments are targeted for early June.
The board ratified the town manager's appointment of a reserve police officer by a 4-0 roll call vote.

why_it_matters: Residents who sit on, or want to join, a town board or committee will face a set notice, written-intent and interview routine each spring, and the public gets a stated chance to comment on reappointments.
The process is not final: the workshop was halted until the two absent members return, so details such as how chairs' input is weighed could still change.
watch_next: The chair's written summary of what was agreed on the appointment process, and the workshop resuming once the full board returns.
The water district superintendent's reply to the invitation to meet March 2 or 9, and the second cannabis outreach meeting on March 10.
